Home » Tax Deed » Tax Deed States » Minnesota Tax Deeds: How to Acquire Discounted Properties » Dakota County

Dakota County sits just south of Saint Paul and forms part of the Twin Cities metro area. It has a mix of city, suburban, and rural land and continues to grow each year. This guide explains how Dakota County tax forfeited tax deed sales work. You will see when auctions happen, how to sign up, and what steps to take as an investor.

What Is Dakota County Tax Deed Investing

Minnesota does not use tax lien certificates. Instead, unpaid property taxes can lead to tax forfeiture. When the redemption period ends, the land passes to the state. Dakota County then offers these parcels through public tax forfeited tax deed auctions. Investors do not earn interest. They buy real property at the sale price and take ownership under the rules of state law.

Important Details

Key Auction Facts at a Glance

Fun Facts About Dakota County

  • Dakota County ranks among the largest Minnesota counties by population.
  • The county seat is Hastings, known for its riverfront location and history.
  • The area includes a mix of urban, suburban, and rural communities.
  • Cities like Lakeville, Eagan, and Apple Valley have seen steady population growth.

Attractions and Economic Highlights

  • Attractions
    • Lebanon Hills Regional Park with lakes, beaches, and long trails
    • Lake Byllesby Regional Park with camping and shoreline access
  • Transportation
    • Strong access through Interstate 35 and other major routes
    • Easy connection to the Twin Cities metro
  • Economy
    • Key industries include health care, retail, and manufacturing
  • Community
    • Many parks, lakes, and outdoor programs all year

Why Dakota County Is Ideal for Tax Deed Investors

  • Large metro area with strong housing demand.
  • Many property types across multiple cities and towns.
  • Tax forfeited sales give investors access to discounted parcels.
  • Returns can rise when purchase price is well below market value.
  • Works well for investors who want a more grounded and low risk investment path.

Auction Process for Tax Deed Sales in Dakota County

Dakota County hosts public auctions for tax forfeited land under state law. These events take place at the Dakota County Administration Center in Hastings. Most sales begin at about 10 a.m. Central Time. Registration usually opens on auction morning and closes before the sale starts.

Bidders compete on price. There is no interest rate to bid down. Some parcels start at a minimum bid equal to past taxes and charges. Others start at an appraised value. The highest bidder wins as long as the final bid meets or exceeds the required minimum.

How the Auction Works

Here is a simple look at how the auction works from registration through deed delivery.

  1. Register for a Bidder Number

    Visit the Administration Center on auction day and register for a bidder number before the sale begins.

  2. Bring Approved Payment

    Bring approved payment methods such as cashier checks or money orders so you are ready if you win.

  3. Take Your Seat Before the Start Time

    Sit in the Board Room before the auction starts and wait for staff instructions.

  4. Listen for Each Parcel and Starting Price

    County staff read each parcel number and the starting price as the sale moves forward.

  5. Bid Until the Final Offer Holds

    Bidders raise cards to offer higher amounts until no higher bid is made and the final bid stands.

  6. Pay by the End of the Business Day

    The top bidder pays the full amount by the end of the business day.

  7. Cover the Added Charges

    Buyers also pay deed tax, recording fees, and other required charges.

  8. Receive the State Quitclaim Deed

    After processing, the buyer receives a state quitclaim deed.

  9. Remember the Sale Is Final

    All parcels sell as is and cannot be returned.

Maximum Potential Returns and Expected Returns on Dakota County Tax Deeds

Your returns come from the spread between the auction price and the value you build later. Some parcels sell for very low amounts, especially small or odd shaped lots. Other parcels may reflect a meaningful discount compared with surrounding land sales.

Your yield depends on research, repairs, cleanup, and resale timing. Many investors compare the return from a tax deed purchase with typical rental income or resale margins in the county. When purchased well, the gains can be strong. The key is to track all extra costs so you see the real profit, not just the gap between winning bid and appraised value.

Open to All Investors and Foreign Investor Participation

Dakota County does not restrict bidders by residency. Anyone who follows the registration rules can attend the sale. Out of state and international buyers often join in person or work through a local representative. Payments must meet county requirements, and buyers must be prepared to pay in full on the same day. International investors should plan ahead for travel, banking, or local representation.

Importance of Due Diligence in Dakota County Tax Deed Investing

Careful research helps you avoid surprises. Dakota County encourages buyers to review parcels before bidding. You take full responsibility for property condition and access once you buy. Good research protects your return and reduces risk.

What Due Diligence Entails

  • Review parcel maps, size, and land use through county tools.
  • Visit the parcel from the street to note access and surroundings.
  • Ask city or county planning staff about building and land use rules.
  • Order a title search to check for surviving liens.
  • Estimate cleanup, holding, and resale costs.
  • Study nearby property values to understand market potential.

Risks of Skipping Due Diligence

  • You might buy a parcel with no access or very limited use.
  • Some parcels may carry special assessments.
  • Some liens can survive forfeiture and may need legal steps to clear.
  • A structure could have major code issues or high repair costs.
  • Your expected profit may drop if you skip research.

Buying Over the Counter Tax Deeds in Dakota County

Dakota County also offers parcels that did not sell during the main auction. These are listed as over the counter properties. Prices are set by the county, and buyers can visit the Property Taxation office to purchase them.

How to Purchase Over the Counter Parcels

  • Review the current list on the county website.
  • Research each parcel before buying.
  • Visit the Property Taxation office during normal hours.
  • Pay the full listed price plus required fees.
  • Receive a receipt and wait for the state deed mailing.

Benefits of Over the Counter Purchases

  • No bidding.
  • More time to study parcels.
  • Useful for buyers who want small lots for extra yard space or future plans.

Why Dakota County Is a Top Choice for Tax Deed Investors

Economic and Tax Advantages

  • Strong job base and stable local economy.
  • Clear county policies on tax forfeited sales.
  • Consistent public notices and easy access to staff for questions.
  • Mix of city and rural areas that offer broad investment options.

Real Estate Market Overview

Dakota County has steady demand in both suburban and rural zones. Parcels in auctions can include small outlots, utility strips, and the occasional larger lot. Investors who understand market pricing can spot good deals and plan clear exit strategies. Many people use these purchases for resale, land holding, or expansion of nearby property.

Conclusion

Dakota County tax forfeited tax deed sales give investors a path to buy property below full market price. Auctions are held at the county Administration Center and follow public rules that are simple to understand. You can also buy over the counter parcels if you prefer a fixed price.

Strong results come from good research. Study each parcel, check land use rules, and stay aware of all costs. With steady growth in the county and many types of parcels, Dakota County can fit well into a long term real estate plan. Smart research helps you build confidence and protect your return on every deal you choose to pursue.

Pro Tips for Dakota County Tax Deed Investors

  • Start with parcels that match your skill level. Smaller lots can be good practice.
  • Check access rights on every parcel. Some smaller lots have limited access.
  • Call city planning offices for any lot you plan to improve.
  • Bring extra money for fees and deed taxes so you are not rushed on auction day.
  • For resale plans, speak with a local agent to understand real demand.

Dakota County Tax Deed FAQs

Can I get title insurance after buying a tax deed

Some title companies may ask for extra steps such as a quiet title action.

Do structures come with safety inspections

No. Buyers should treat all buildings as unsafe until inspected.

Can I rent out the property right away

You need to meet local code rules first.

Can I bid with a loan

Funds must clear on the same day. Prepare money before the auction.

What if someone lives on the property I buy

You must follow state rules on notice and removal. Speak with an attorney.
